svg.title: Ordering a prompt so the cache can reuse its prefix
svg.desc: On the left, the parts of a TaskFlow project Q and A request stacked in the order they are sent: tool definitions and instructions, both stable for the whole deployment; the project documents at version 12, stable per project, ending with an explicit breakpoint kept for 12 hours; the conversation history, which grows by appending and has an implicit or automatic breakpoint at its end; and the new question, which changes on every request. A bracket marks the first four parts as the cacheable prefix and the question as uncached. On the right, what each kind of change invalidates: editing a tool schema makes everything miss; editing the instructions invalidates the instructions and everything after; a new docs version invalidates the documents and everything after; appending a turn invalidates nothing because the prefix is kept; a new question is the only new part. A red box shows the anti-pattern of putting the current time in the instructions, which changes the first block on every request and produces zero cache hits.

g.text: Request, in the order it is sent
stable per project; explicit breakpoint at the end, 12 h
grows by appending; implicit or automatic breakpoint
edit a tool schema: everything misses
edit the instructions: they and all later parts miss
new docs version: docs and all later parts miss
append a turn: nothing misses, the prefix is kept
new question: the only part processed at full price
Anti-pattern: "Current time: 14:05:12" in the instructions changes the first block on every request, so nothing is ever reused.
Order the prompt from most stable to least stable; a cache can only reuse an unchanged prefix.
